title: Self Evaluation
description: The check-point lesson that looks back on the first five lessons and turns them into language: building any question with the three systematised formulas (WH word + am/is/are/was/were + subject, WH word + did + subject + base verb, WH word + do/does + subject + base verb) and answering with positive and negative short answers that repeat the helper of the question (Yes, I do. / No, I don't. / Yes, she was. / No, she wasn't. / Yes, they have. / No, they haven't.); the language of self-evaluation itself — saying how difficult a lesson was (I found it easy / fairly difficult), how long a text was (too long, the right length), how interesting a topic was, how much you understood, naming a strong point and a difficulty with good at and not very good at + a noun or an -ing verb, then agreeing with a partner on one common strong point and one common difficulty and reporting them to the class with we and our; the five ways of making a suggestion and what each one is followed by (Why not + base verb, What about + noun or -ing verb, You should + base verb, You could + base verb, If you + present..., you will...), with the difference between a friendly offer, strong advice and a possibility; taking a resolution with will ('ll, won't, base verb, and the overlap with going to); and the end-of-chapter research task preparing lesson 10, six guide questions on Ibn Khaldun for the pupil to investigate
sources: Official programme sheet — English, first year of secondary education (common core), CNP Tunisia: .claude/skills/content-ecole-tn/references/programmes-officiels/programme/1ere-sec/anglais.md (lesson 6, "Self evaluation")
